scope: Preserve scheduled workflow occurrence identity through storage, connection and launch-response failures; expose readable recovery controls, theme-aware workflow surfaces and accurate unavailable-credential state.
implementation: Persist a frozen occurrence and a dispatch marker before its first start request; advance only after a validated engine confirmation and acknowledged local tracking write.

Recover potentially submitted occurrences using GET on their original engine and deterministic workflow ID; missing, conflicting, malformed or timed-out responses never authorize a fresh start request.
Guard launches against configuration generation changes, pending saves, pause/edit intent and unmount; serialize collection writes and merge only user changes into the latest schedule.
Preserve terminal tracking receipts and acknowledged local state; catch secondary persistence failures and retain accepted action/fleet outcomes without resending accepted command drafts.
Show pending/preparing/attention states with original-engine guidance, Check/Retry controls, caught save errors and protected deletion/Run now actions.
Distinguish unavailable saved key/connection state from a confirmed missing key across workflow and computer-chat settings.
Give schedule identity and status a full-width wrapping row above its controls; use semantic surfaces, borders and readable muted text in both themes.
Use the existing semantic primary button treatment for workflow launch, attach and save actions; scan the workflow header as well as the pending schedule in both themes.

Native owned-profile process restart retains pending identity after HTTP404, then saves terminal confirmation using two scoped GET requests and zero start POSTs; retains dark/light screenshots. The owned bootstrap explicitly selects the real memory-only credential fallback, asserts its key is absent after restart, then restores it through the normal bridge.

verification.queue_qualification: Integrated and native phases share one sequential Buildr admission when their job IDs match.

previous_focused_pass.qualification: Passed before the final confirmed-manual-launch recovery and nullable run-ID type correction; superseded by the final combined gate.

previous_integrated_pass.qualification: Passed before screenshot review exposed cramped schedule names and opaque light-theme panels. Superseded by the final semantic layout, scoped accessibility checks and unique toast-ID test fixtures.

previous_design_pass.qualification: Schedule-row checks passed; visual review then found an omitted light-theme primary label outside that scan. Superseded by semantic primary buttons, expanded header scans and stable pre-scan captures. The earlier capture alone does not establish the rendering cause.

earlier_native_timeout.qualification: The focused checks passed, but native setup exceeded the unchanged 60-second test budget before any layout/recovery assertion. Its retained trace shows about 45 seconds in the native credential-read IPC after a 15-second initial storage/key setup. The final owned fixture selects the real memory-only credential backend before importing main; no product behavior, test timeout or recovery assertion was weakened. This is not a queue failure or evidence of final acceptance.

earlier_fixture_traffic_failure.qualification: Header/schedule Axe scans and layout checks passed, then the pre-Check traffic assertion saw two unauthenticated GET / requests. Their caller is unproven and the workflow client does not use that route. The final fixture retains such root-only reads separately while keeping every POST and all other requests in the exact workflow assertions. Native reports, trace and captures remain preserved; this attempt is not final acceptance.

preserved_prior_native_job.qualification: Different frozen updater source completed with its already-corrected Electron AxeBuilder Target.createTarget harness error; not evidence against or acceptance of this candidate.

earlier_typechecks.qualification: New-code TypeScript narrowing/nullability and test selector-option errors stopped these runs before tests. Corrected in the final verified source; not queue failures.

checks: Real repository Vite test configuration, single worker

scoped_accessibility.scope: Workflow header and pending schedule row with their controls
scoped_accessibility.qualification: Scoped scans do not establish whole-application accessibility certification.

layout_assertions: Schedule name is not horizontally clipped
Schedule section uses the semantic surface token
native.traffic_evidence: scheduled-recovery-requests JSON attachment retains two exact workflow status GETs, separately counted unauthenticated GET / probes, and primary-button computed-style diagnostics before/after each scan. All POSTs and all other requests remain in strict workflow assertions.
native.qualification: Controlled native profile/HTTP fixture. Its owned bootstrap selects the real memory-only credential fallback; key absence after restart and re-entry through the normal bridge are asserted. This case does not consult or establish host OS keyring behavior.

request_receipt.qualification: Computed style checks preserve visible button text before/after the scoped Axe scan; this does not replace the test's accessibility analysis.

native.visual_review: Reviewed the exact retained dark/light captures after the final pass: schedule names, status and primary labels are readable. Earlier unstable captures did not establish a CSS or Axe cause; final captures wait for fonts and two frames before accessibility instrumentation.

source_guard.qualification: Manual hashes before/after checks, not an immutable queue snapshot.

dependency_audit.qualification: Unchanged package/lock bytes retain the prior source-bound audit (production 0, development 15 affected-package entries). This is not a fresh full audit; the new exact-head CI production gate is required.

verification.full_ci: Required on the next committed source. Focused checks do not establish all platform/bundle/installer acceptance.

limitations: Controlled tests and the local engine source contract do not establish live engine/Temporal/sandbox/provider/NSR acceptance or an indefinite exactly-once guarantee.
A submitted occurrence that the engine cannot confirm remains pending for operator recovery; status absence does not prove that no execution occurred.
The request observation timeout does not cancel work already admitted by the engine.
Required signing and live acceptance remain gated; immutable v1.1.20 stays at fe2f9d6 and this branch work is unreleased.
